etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Ancient Greek στρατηγία (stratēgía, “office of general, command, generalship”), from στρατηγός (stratēgós, “the leader or commander of an army, a general”), from στρατός (stratós, “army”) + ἄγω (ágō, “I lead, I conduct”).

definitions.definition: (uncountable) The science and art of military command as applied to the overall planning and conduct of warfare.

quote.citation: 1913, Robert Barr, chapter 4, in Lord Stranleigh Abroad‎[1]:
quote.text: “I came down like a wolf on the fold, didn’t I ?  Why didn’t I telephone ?  Strategy, my dear boy, strategy. This is a surprise attack, and I’d no wish that the garrison, forewarned, should escape. …”

definitions.definition: (countable) A plan of action intended to accomplish a specific goal.

quote.citation: 2013 May-June, William E. Conner, “An Acoustic Arms Race”, in American Scientist, volume 101, number 3, pages 206–7:
quote.text: Earless ghost swift moths become “invisible” to echolocating bats by forming mating clusters close […] above vegetation and effectively blending into the clutter of echoes that the bat receives from the leaves and stems around them. Many insects probably use this strategy, which is a close analogy to crypsis in the visible world—camouflage and other methods for blending into one’s visual background.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) The act of strategizing; the development of effective strategies.
